title: Policy Rule
description: One tenant-authored rule within a Policy version: where it is evaluated, what it yields, and the conditions under which it matches.
$comment: Normative prose: 40-governance/policy-model.md. The match member is one CEL expression under the Orchestra Expression Profile, yielding a boolean (ADR-0035); the profile, not this file, defines its inputs, functions and cost bound. It stays unconstrained here, because constraining a member this version left open would tighten an existing constraint, which VERSIONING section 6 forbids for a MINOR change, so publication refuses a rule that does not parse, type-check or stay within the cost bound. This file fixes the envelope a rule lives in — scope, enforcement point, verdict, versioning. Rule precedence is order-independent: any deny wins, otherwise any require_approval wins and every matching rule's chain is required, otherwise allow, and no matching rule is deny. The verdict is a function of which rules match and never of their order, so no member orders rules. Tenant-scoped and Workspace-scoped rules are evaluated together under that precedence.

policy_id.description: The Policy this rule belongs to.

version.description: Assigned and frozen by publication, never authored. A draft carries none.
version.$comment: P5 — a Policy is immutably versioned on the same terms as Agent and Workflow definitions (VERSIONING sections 2 and 8, W1 to W4). Editing a Policy means publishing a new version. A published version MUST be retained at least as long as any Audit Record referencing it.

tenant_id.description: Mandatory. A Policy MUST NOT be evaluated against another Tenant's inputs.
tenant_id.$comment: P2 and invariant I1 — isolation is enforced by row-level security in the datastore, not by application code (ADR-0011).

workspace_id.description: Optional administrative scope. A Workspace scopes administration and visibility, never isolation.
workspace_id.$comment: ADR-0035 — an evaluation in a Workspace considers the rules that name it together with the Tenant's rules that name no Workspace, under one precedence, so a rule naming a Workspace can add a deny or a gate and never remove a Tenant's.

name.description: Author-assigned name, for diagnosis and for the audit surface.

enforcement_points.description: The enforcement points at which this rule is evaluated.
enforcement_points.$comment: E1 fixes the minimum set — Run admission, every Workflow Step boundary, and before any Tool invocation — and calls it a minimum, not a maximum. A later document may add an enforcement point; none of these three may be removed without superseding that section. Adding a member here is MINOR under VERSIONING R2, unlike the verdict set below.

verdict.description: What this rule yields when it matches. An evaluation yields exactly one verdict: never two, never none.
verdict.$comment: P3 — the verdict set is closed. There is no warn, no allow-with-conditions, no silent pass-through. A fourth verdict is NOT the additive case VERSIONING R2 makes MINOR: the set is exhaustive and every consumer branches across all of it, so a new value repurposes the enum rather than adding one a consumer may ignore under R3. It is MAJOR and needs an ADR. One narrowing exists and is not expressible here: at the boundary of an approval Step the set narrows to require_approval and deny, and an implementation MUST NOT return allow there (V4) — a constraint on the evaluation, not on what a rule may be authored to yield.

match.description: One CEL expression under the Expression Profile, yielding a boolean: true when this rule applies. Checked at publication rather than by this schema — see this file's top-level comment.
match.$comment: policy-model.md N1 fixes what every evaluation receives and a rule MAY match on: the Principal and its subtype, the Tenant, the Workspace, the pinned definition version, the pinned Policy versions, the Step and its type at a Step boundary, the Side-Effect Class as a primary input, the Tool, its schema major, its Tool Catalog registration state, the Tools the pinned version declares and the capability grants naming its definition, the proposed action including its arguments, the origin labels of those arguments and of the data the action references, the enforcement point, and the Run. A Step's Side-Effect Class is derived at publication and is a set at an agent or subworkflow Step's boundary (ADR-0045); an origin label says where a value came from — admission input, definition literal, Tool result, retrieved content, model output or UI Action text — and never that it is safe (ADR-0044). A restriction on what a Tool call may do — an amount, a region, a record — is written here, as a match on the proposed action's arguments, and never as a condition on a capability grant (ADR-0042, policy-model.md S2). N3 requires any input outside that table — the evaluation time, the value read from an aggregate — to be captured in the Policy Decision, and a rule reads aggregate state only through an aggregate the platform defines, reserved in the transaction that writes the decision (ADR-0035). An expression that raises an error does not make its rule a non-match: the evaluation has not completed, and A3 forbids allow. D4 forbids a model in the evaluation path: a model call is neither deterministic nor attributable to a rule.

approval.description: The Approval Chain, and the optional decision deadline, that an Approval Request raised under this rule takes.
approval.$comment: ADR-0043 and approval-workflows.md sections 5 to 7. A rule under which a request can be raised declares a chain: one whose verdict is require_approval, or one whose allow V4 narrows to require_approval at the boundary of an approval Step. The schema cannot require the member without tightening v1. Where several matching rules return require_approval, one Approval Request carries every one of their chains and none stands in for another, and the shortest decision_deadline any of them declares applies (C9, ADR-0035). Where no matching rule declares a chain, the gate has no position, could never be satisfied, and the request is refused at raise rather than raised (C10). The Tenant authors every figure here.

chain.description: Whether the chain is ordered or parallel, and its positions.

positions.description: The chain's positions, in order where the chain is ordered.

eligible.description: Which Platform Users are eligible at this position, resolved when a request is raised. Unconstrained, like match and for the same reason: it is written in the policy language, which is not defined here.
eligible.$comment: Whatever it resolves to, a Principal who is not a Platform User is never eligible (C5), nor is the Principal the Run records at admission, nor anyone standing on the same verified Person as them (C13, C15), and no Policy can override any of it (C16).

required_positions.description: For a parallel chain, how many of its positions must be satisfied. Absent means every position. An ordered chain omits it.

decision_deadline.description: How long a request raised under this rule may stay Pending before it expires, as an ISO 8601 duration. Absent means no deadline.
decision_deadline.$comment: ADR-0043. The deadline runs from the raise, and expiry resolves the request Expired as an observed condition that records its cause and no Principal. There is no re-raise. Orchestra sets no default and no bound.

description.description: Author-supplied prose. Explains the rule; never constrains it.
